name: Dengue Fever
overview: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV, serotypes 1-4) transmitted through the bite of infected female Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. It presents acutely with severe flu-like illness.
causes: Dengue virus infection (Flavivirus family)
Bite of infected day-biting Aedes mosquitoes
transmission: Transmitted primarily through mosquito bites
Non-contagious from human to human by casual contact
Mosquitoes breed in clean standing water in containers
risk_factors: Living in or traveling to tropical and subtropical climates
Previous dengue infection (elevates risk of severe dengue/DHF)
prevention: Eliminate standing water in discarded containers, flower pots, tires, and cooler tanks
Use mosquito repellents containing DEET, Picaridin, or Oil of Lemon Eucalyptus
Install wire mesh screens on doors and windows
Wear long-sleeved light-colored clothing
Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets
general_care_information: Strict bed rest during the acute febrile phase
Drink plenty of fluids (3 to 4 liters daily: ORS, tender coconut water, fresh fruit juices) to prevent hemoconcentration
Use only Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) for fever and pain relief
Monitor platelet counts and hematocrit daily through routine CBC blood tests
warning_signs: Severe persistent abdominal pain or tenderness
Persistent vomiting (unable to retain fluids)
Mucosal bleeding (bleeding gums, epistaxis / nosebleeds, black stools)
Lethargy, extreme restlessness, or mental confusion
Sudden temperature drop accompanied by cold, clammy skin (dengue shock syndrome)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek immediate hospital emergency admission if any warning sign appears, if platelets fall below 100,000/μL, or if signs of fluid leakage or shock develop.
contraindications: STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: Do NOT take Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Naproxen, or other NSAIDs as they severely aggravate bleeding and platelet dysfunction.

faqs.q: Can dengue be treated with antibiotics?
faqs.a: No. Dengue is caused by a virus, so antibiotics have no effect. Treatment focuses on supportive care, rigorous hydration, and monitoring.

faqs.q: How can I tell dengue apart from malaria?
faqs.a: Dengue typically features retro-orbital eye pain, flushed face, and rash, whereas malaria features cyclical rigors/chills with sweating stages and is diagnosed via peripheral blood smear.

hi.name: डेंगू बुखार
hi.overview: एडीज मच्छर के काटने से फैलने वाला वायरल संक्रमण जिसमें अचानक तेज बुखार और गंभीर जोड़ों का दर्द होता है।

te.name: డెంగ్యూ జ్వరం
te.overview: ఏడిస్ దోమ కాటు ద్వారా వ్యాపించే వైరల్ ఇన్ఫెక్షన్. తీవ్రమైన జ్వరం మరియు కీళ్ల నొప్పులు దీని ప్రధాన లక్షణాలు.

name: Malaria
overview: Malaria is a life-threatening protozoan infection caused by Plasmodium parasites (P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale) transmitted to humans through the nocturnal bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
causes: Plasmodium parasite invasion of liver and erythrocytes (red blood cells)
transmission: Night-biting female Anopheles mosquito bites
Rarely through blood transfusion or organ transplant
risk_factors: Living in warm tropical areas with poor drainage
Stagnant pools, ponds, and puddles near homes
prevention: Sleep under long-lasting insecticide-treated nets (LLINs)
Indoor residual spraying (IRS) with approved insecticides
Apply mosquito repellents during dusk and night hours
Eliminate water pooling around residences
Take chemoprophylaxis when advised by doctors before visiting high-transmission areas
general_care_information: Confirmed diagnosis via rapid diagnostic test (RDT) or peripheral blood smear
Complete the entire course of physician-prescribed antimalarial medications (such as Artemisinin-based combination therapies - ACT)
Maintain high fluid intake to prevent dehydration
Tepid sponging and paracetamol for temperature management
warning_signs: Impaired consciousness, delirium, or seizures (Cerebral Malaria)
Extreme pallor, jaundice, or deep yellow urine
Respiratory distress or rapid shallow breathing
Inability to sit upright or swallow liquids
when_to_seek_medical_help: Immediate medical admission is mandatory if high cyclical fever occurs after visiting an endemic region, or if any sign of cerebral or falciparum malaria arises.
contraindications: Do not delay confirmatory testing; untreated P. falciparum can be fatal within 24 hours.

faqs.q: Is malaria contagious directly from person to person?
faqs.a: No, malaria cannot be transmitted casually, through coughing, sneezing, or physical contact.

faqs.q: Can malaria recur after treatment?
faqs.a: Yes, P. vivax and P. ovale have dormant liver stages (hypnozoites) that can cause relapses months later unless treated with primaquine.

hi.name: मलेरिया
hi.overview: मादा एनोफिलीज मच्छर के काटने से फैलने वाला परजीवी संक्रमण, जिसमें कंपकंपी के साथ तेज बुखार आता है।

te.name: మలేరియా
te.overview: ఆడ అనాఫిలిస్ దోమ కాటు వల్ల వచ్చే పరాన్నజీవి వ్యాధి. చలితో కూడిన తీవ్ర జ్వరం దీని ప్రధాన లక్షణం.

name: Tuberculosis (TB)
overview: Tuberculosis is a potentially serious infectious bacterial disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that primarily attacks the lungs (pulmonary TB), but can also affect kidneys, spine, and brain (extrapulmonary TB).
common_symptoms: Chronic cough lasting more than 2-3 weeks
Hemoptysis (coughing up blood or blood-streaked sputum)
causes: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection inhaled via airborne droplets
transmission: Airborne transmission when a person with active pulmonary TB coughs, sneezes, speaks, or spits
risk_factors: Compromised immune system (HIV, diabetes, malnutrition, immunosuppressive therapy)
Crowded or poorly ventilated living environments
Close contact with active untreated TB patients
prevention: BCG (Bacille Calmette-Guérin) vaccination in infants
Ensuring good natural ventilation and sunlight in living spaces
Cough hygiene: covering mouth and nose with a tissue or elbow
Prompt diagnosis and completed treatment of index cases to stop transmission chain
Preventive therapy for close household contacts when clinically advised
general_care_information: Undergo Directly Observed Therapy (DOTS) under national TB elimination guidelines
Take all prescribed antibiotics (e.g. Isoniazid, Rifampicin, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol) strictly every day for the full 6-9 month duration
High-protein, nutritious diet with adequate calories and micronutrients to rebuild body mass
Never stop medication early even if symptoms disappear completely
warning_signs: Massive hemoptysis (large volume coughing of blood)
Severe shortness of breath or cyanosis (bluish lips)
Severe persistent drug reaction (jaundice, vision changes, intense rash)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Consult a healthcare center immediately for sputum testing and chest X-ray if you have had a cough lasting over 2 weeks with unexplained weight loss or night sweats.
contraindications: Never skip doses or discontinue anti-TB medications prematurely; doing so leads to Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB).

faqs.q: Is TB completely curable?
faqs.a: Yes! TB is 100% curable if the full prescribed regimen of antibiotics is taken consistently without interruption.

faqs.q: Can latent TB spread to others?
faqs.a: No. People with latent TB infection have no symptoms and cannot spread the bacteria to others.

hi.name: तपेदिक / टीबी (Tuberculosis)
hi.overview: माइकोबैक्टीरियम ट्यूबरकुलोसिस बैक्टीरिया से होने वाला संक्रामक फेफड़ों का रोग।

te.name: క్షయ వ్యాధి (టీబీ)
te.overview: మైకోబాక్టీరియం ట్యూబర్‌క్యులోసిస్ వల్ల కలిగే ఊపిరితిత్తుల అంటువ్యాధి. 2 వారాలకు మించి దగ్గు దీని లక్షణం.

name: Typhoid Fever
overview: Typhoid fever is an acute systemic infection caused by the bacterium Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi. It is characterized by persistent step-ladder high fever, gastrointestinal disturbance, and toxemia.
common_symptoms: Rose spots (faint pink rash on chest and abdomen)
causes: Ingestion of food, milk, or water contaminated with Salmonella Typhi feces or urine
transmission: Fecal-oral route through contaminated drinking water, street food, unwashed raw produce, or infected food handlers
risk_factors: Lack of clean potable water supply
Eating uncooked food from hygiene-compromised sources
prevention: Drink only boiled, filtered, or sealed bottled water
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before eating and after using toilets
Avoid street foods, unpasteurized milk, ice from unknown sources, and cut fruits left in the open
Typhoid conjugate vaccination (TCV) for children and travellers
Ensure safe sewage disposal and toilet sanitation
general_care_information: Confirmatory blood culture test or Widal serology
Complete full course of antibiotics prescribed by an attending physician
High-calorie, easily digestible soft diet (khichdi, curd rice, boiled potatoes, soups)
Frequent oral rehydration therapy to replenish fluid and electrolyte loss
warning_signs: Sudden severe abdominal pain with rigidity (intestinal perforation danger)
Rectal bleeding or dark tarry stools
Persistent high fever with delirium or extreme apathy (typhoid state)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek immediate hospital care if fever exceeds 4-5 days without remission, or if acute abdominal rigidity or severe bleeding develops.
contraindications: Avoid spicy, oily, or fibrous foods during recovery as they irritate inflamed Peyer's patches.

faqs.q: Can someone carry typhoid without feeling sick?
faqs.a: Yes, chronic asymptomatic carriers can harbor Salmonella Typhi in their gallbladders and shed bacteria in stools for years.

faqs.q: Is boiling water effective against typhoid bacteria?
faqs.a: Yes, vigorous boiling for at least 1-2 minutes kills Salmonella Typhi and makes water safe.

hi.name: टाइफाइड / मियादी बुखार
hi.overview: दूषित पानी या भोजन से साल्मोनेला टाइफी बैक्टीरिया द्वारा फैलने वाला आंतों का गंभीर संक्रमण।

te.name: టైఫాయిడ్ జ్వరం
te.overview: కలుషిత నీరు, ఆహారం వల్ల సాల్మొనెల్లా టైఫీ బ్యాక్టీరియాతో వచ్చే వ్యాధి. నిరంతర తీవ్ర జ్వరం దీని ప్రధాన లక్షణం.

name: Cholera
overview: Cholera is an extremely virulent bacterial infection caused by ingestion of food or water contaminated with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. It can cause severe acute watery diarrhea and rapid hypovolemic shock within hours.
common_symptoms: Extreme thirst and dry mucous membranes
Rapid heart rate and low blood pressure
Painful muscle cramps due to electrolyte depletion
causes: Vibrio cholerae colonization of the small intestine producing cholera enterotoxin
transmission: Drinking sewage-contaminated water
Eating seafood from contaminated waters or raw contaminated food
risk_factors: Monsoon flooding and damaged sanitation infrastructure
prevention: Use only water treated with chlorine tablets, boiled, or safely filtered
Practice rigorous hand washing with soap before handling meals
Cook foods thoroughly and eat them while hot
Oral cholera vaccines (OCV) for high-risk and outbreak populations
Proper disinfection of latrines and disposal of patient stools
general_care_information: IMMEDIATE ORAL REHYDRATION SALTS (ORS) administration at the very onset
Intravenous fluids (Ringer's lactate) for severe dehydration
Continue zinc supplementation in children to decrease diarrhea duration
Physician-directed antibiotics (e.g. Azithromycin, Doxycycline) in moderate to severe cases
warning_signs: Anuria (zero urine output for over 6 hours)
Sunken eyes, lethargy, or unconsciousness
Rapid, feeble, or unpalpable peripheral pulse
Cyanosis and cold clammy skin (severe hypovolemic shock)
when_to_seek_medical_help: EMERGENCY: Proceed to the nearest hospital or emergency clinic immediately upon experiencing continuous watery diarrhea. Delaying rehydration can be fatal within hours.
contraindications: Never withhold fluids; do not rely on plain water alone without electrolytes in severe cholera as it can trigger hyponatremic seizures.

faqs.q: Can cholera kill within a single day?
faqs.a: Yes, severe untreated cholera can cause fatal dehydration and kidney failure within 6 to 12 hours. Rapid rehydration saves over 99% of patients.

hi.name: हैजा (Cholera)
hi.overview: विब्रियो कोलेरी बैक्टीरिया से होने वाला घातक दस्त रोग, जिससे कुछ ही घंटों में गंभीर डिहाइड्रेशन हो सकता है।

te.name: కలరా
te.overview: కలుషిత నీరు తాగడం వల్ల వైబ్రియో కలరా బ్యాక్టీరియాతో వచ్చే తీవ్ర నీళ్ల విరేచనాలు. వెంటనే ఓఆర్ఎస్ తీసుకోవాలి.

name: COVID-19
overview: COVID-19 is a contagious respiratory illness caused by the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), ranging from mild upper respiratory symptoms to severe pneumonia and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).
common_symptoms: Sudden loss of taste (ageusia) or smell (anosmia)
causes: SARS-CoV-2 viral infection of respiratory epithelial cells via ACE2 receptors
transmission: Airborne inhalation of respiratory aerosols and droplets expelled during breathing, speaking, singing, or coughing
Touching contaminated surfaces and then touching mouth, eyes, or nose
risk_factors: Pre-existing comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, chronic lung disease, obesity)
Crowded indoor environments with poor ventilation
prevention: Up-to-date COVID-19 vaccination and booster doses
Wearing well-fitted N95 / KN95 masks in crowded or enclosed settings
Ensuring cross-ventilation and air filtration indoors
Frequent hand hygiene with alcohol rub or soap
Isolating when experiencing acute respiratory symptoms
general_care_information: Monitor blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) 3-4 times daily using a pulse oximeter
Adequate hydration, warm fluid intake, and steam inhalation
Paracetamol for fever and body aches
Prone positioning (lying on the stomach) to improve oxygenation if dyspneic under medical guidance
warning_signs: Blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) falling below 93% on room air
Persistent pressure or heavy pain in the chest
Severe difficulty breathing or rapid gasping
Confusion, inability to awaken, or bluish lips / nail beds (cyanosis)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek emergency medical care if SpO2 drops below 94%, if breathing becomes labored, or if fever persists continuously beyond 5 days.
contraindications: Do NOT self-medicate with systemic steroids or antibiotics without explicit prescription from a licensed medical professional.

faqs.q: What is normal SpO2 on room air?
faqs.a: A healthy resting SpO2 is between 95% and 100%. Readings consistently below 94% require medical evaluation.

hi.name: कोविड-19 (COVID-19)
hi.overview: सार्स-सीओवी-2 वायरस से फैलने वाला संक्रामक श्वसन रोग जिसमें बुखार, खांसी और सांस लेने में कठिनाई हो सकती है।

te.name: కోవిడ్-19
te.overview: కరోనా వైరస్ వల్ల కలిగే శ్వాసకోశ ఇన్ఫెక్షన్. జ్వరం, పొడి దగ్గు, వాసన/రుచి కోల్పోవడం దీని ప్రధాన లక్షణాలు.

name: Influenza (Flu)
overview: Influenza is an acute contagious viral respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses (types A, B, and C) that infects the nose, throat, and sometimes the lungs, presenting abruptly with high fever and prostration.
common_symptoms: Severe muscle, joint, and body aches
Sore throat and clear runny nose
causes: Influenza type A and B viruses circulating seasonally
transmission: Inhaling respiratory droplets when infected individuals cough, sneeze, or talk
Contact with contaminated hands or surfaces followed by touching eyes or mouth
risk_factors: Young children under 5 and adults over 65
Asthma, COPD, heart disease, diabetes, or immunosuppression
prevention: Annual seasonal influenza vaccination
Covering coughs and sneezes with disposable tissues or flexed elbow
Frequent handwashing with soap and water
Staying home from school or work when symptomatic to avoid community spread
Avoiding close contact with sick individuals
general_care_information: Ample rest and sleep to allow immune recovery
High fluid intake: warm broths, herbal teas, electrolyte solutions
Saline nasal drops and warm salt water gargles for throat discomfort
Paracetamol for fever and pain; antiviral medications (such as Oseltamivir) if prescribed early within 48 hours for high-risk patients
warning_signs: Shortness of breath or rapid breathing
Chest pain or heaviness
Fever returning after initially subsiding (suggestive of secondary bacterial pneumonia)
Severe dizziness, drowsiness, or confusion
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek medical attention if breathing difficulties arise, or if high-risk individuals (pregnant, elderly, asthmatics) contract symptoms.
contraindications: Never give Aspirin to children or adolescents with flu-like symptoms due to the risk of Reye's syndrome (fatal hepatic and cerebral failure).

faqs.q: How does the flu differ from a common cold?
faqs.a: Flu comes on abruptly with high fever, severe body aches, and prostration; a cold begins gradually with runny nose and mild sore throat without severe prostration.

hi.name: इन्फ्लुएंजा / फ्लू (Influenza)
hi.overview: इन्फ्लुएंजा वायरस से होने वाला तीव्र श्वसन संक्रमण, जिसमें अचानक तेज बुखार और तेज बदन दर्द होता है।

te.name: ఇన్‌ఫ్లుయెంజా (ఫ్లూ)
te.overview: వైరస్ వల్ల అకస్మాత్తుగా వచ్చే శ్వాసకోశ ఇన్ఫెక్షన్. తీవ్రమైన ఒళ్లు నొప్పులు మరియు జ్వరం ఉంటాయి.

name: Bronchial Asthma
overview: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways characterized by hyper-responsiveness, reversible airflow obstruction, and bronchospasm leading to recurrent episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, and chest tightness.
common_symptoms: Expiratory wheezing (musical whistling sound during exhalation)
Chronic coughing (especially at night or early morning)
Difficulty speaking in complete sentences during attacks
causes: Chronic airway inflammation and bronchoconstriction triggered by genetic predisposition and environmental triggers
transmission: Non-communicable chronic disease; cannot be transmitted from person to person
risk_factors: Family history of asthma or atopy (eczema, allergic rhinitis)
Environmental allergens (dust mites, pollen, pet dander, mold)
prevention: Identify and strictly avoid personal asthma triggers (cold air, dust, smoke, pet fur, strong scents)
Use allergen-proof mattress and pillow covers to minimize dust mites
Avoid active and passive cigarette smoking
Keep emergency rescue inhaler (Salbutamol) readily accessible at all times
Maintain consistent controller medication (inhaled corticosteroids) as prescribed
general_care_information: Use peak flow meters at home to track airway patency
Master proper inhaler and spacer technique for optimal drug delivery into small bronchi
Maintain an Asthma Action Plan developed with your pulmonologist
Perform gentle breathing exercises (Pursed-lip breathing)
warning_signs: Inability to speak more than 1-2 words between breaths
Chest wall retractions (sucking in of skin between ribs and above collarbones)
Peak expiratory flow (PEF) below 50% of personal best
No improvement 10 minutes after using rescue inhaler puffs
Silent chest (complete cessation of wheezing due to zero air movement - fatal emergency)
when_to_seek_medical_help: EMERGENCY: Call 108 or go to the nearest emergency department immediately if rescue inhaler fails to relieve dyspnea or if speech is interrupted by breathlessness.
contraindications: Do NOT delay using rescue inhaler (Salbutamol); avoid Beta-blockers and NSAIDs which can trigger severe fatal bronchospasm in sensitive asthmatics.

faqs.q: Are asthma inhalers addictive?
faqs.a: No. Inhalers are not addictive; they deliver tiny, precise micro-doses directly to lung airways with minimal systemic absorption.

hi.name: दमा / अस्थमा (Asthma)
hi.overview: श्वासनलियों की पुरानी सूजन जिसमें सांस फूलना, छाती में जकड़न और घरघराहट की आवाज होती है।

te.name: ఆస్తమా / ఉబ్బసం
te.overview: శ్వాసనాళాల వాపు వల్ల వచ్చే దీర్ఘకాలిక సమస్య. పిల్లికూతలు, ఆయాసం, శ్వాస తీసుకోవడంలో ఇబ్బంది ఉంటాయి.

name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
overview: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic metabolic condition characterized by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency, resulting in chronic hyperglycemia (elevated blood glucose levels) that progressively damages micro- and macro-vascular systems.
common_symptoms: Tingling or numbness in feet (peripheral neuropathy)
causes: Insulin resistance in peripheral tissues coupled with pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction
transmission: Non-communicable chronic metabolic disease
risk_factors: Sedentary lifestyle with minimal physical activity
History of gestational diabetes or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
Diet high in refined carbohydrates and sugary beverages
prevention: Maintain healthy body weight (BMI between 18.5 and 23 for South Asian populations)
Engage in at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walking, cycling) per week
Adopt a balanced plate: 50% fiber-rich vegetables, 25% lean protein, 25% complex whole grains
Eliminate sugary sodas, refined flours, sweets, and ultra-processed snacks
Routine screening: annual Fasting Blood Sugar (FBS) and HbA1c testing after age 30
general_care_information: Regular self-monitoring of blood glucose (glucometer) and 3-monthly HbA1c testing (target usually < 7.0%)
Daily foot examination: inspect for blisters, cracks, cuts, or redness; never walk barefoot
Strict adherence to prescribed oral hypoglycemic agents (e.g. Metformin) or insulin
Annual dilated eye exam, kidney microalbuminuria urine test, and cardiovascular checkups
warning_signs: Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State (HHS) / Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): extreme dehydration, confusion, sweet fruity breath
Hypoglycemia (blood sugar < 70 mg/dL): trembling, cold sweat, palpitations, dizziness, confusion (requires immediate 15g fast sugar intake)
Non-healing foot ulcer with redness or blackening (gangrene risk)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Consult your physician regularly for glycemic management. Seek emergency care immediately if blood sugar is < 55 mg/dL with altered sensorium or > 350 mg/dL with dehydration.
contraindications: Never abruptly discontinue insulin or diabetes medications without medical guidance; doing so can precipitate life-threatening ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar coma.

faqs.q: What is a healthy fasting blood sugar range?
faqs.a: Normal fasting glucose is 70–99 mg/dL. 100–125 mg/dL indicates prediabetes, and 126 mg/dL or higher on two tests indicates diabetes.

hi.name: टाइप 2 मधुमेह / शुगर (Diabetes)
hi.overview: क्रोनिक मेटाबॉलिक रोग जिसमें इंसुलिन प्रतिरोध के कारण रक्त शर्करा (ब्लड शुगर) का स्तर बढ़ जाता है।

te.name: మధుమేహం / డయాబెటిస్
te.overview: రక్తంలో చక్కెర స్థాయిలు ఎక్కువగా ఉండే జీవక్రియ సమస్య. అధిక దాహం, తరచుగా మూత్రవిసర్జన ప్రధాన లక్షణాలు.

name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
overview: Hypertension is a chronic cardiovascular condition in which the systemic arterial blood pressure is persistently elevated (systolic BP ≥ 140 mmHg and/or diastolic BP ≥ 90 mmHg). It is known as the 'Silent Killer' because it typically progresses without overt symptoms for years.
common_symptoms: Often asymptomatic in early to moderate stages
Morning occipital headaches (throbbing pain at base of skull)
Pulsatile tinnitus (buzzing or whooshing sound in ears)
Shortness of breath upon mild exertion
causes: Primary (essential) hypertension: multifactorial genetic, dietary, vascular stiffness, and autonomic factors
Secondary hypertension: renal artery stenosis, kidney disease, endocrine tumors
transmission: Non-communicable chronic cardiovascular disease
risk_factors: Lack of regular physical activity and obesity
Excessive alcohol consumption and tobacco use
Advancing age and family history of early stroke or heart attack
prevention: Follow the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet rich in vegetables, fruits, and low-fat dairy
Limit table salt to less than 1 level teaspoon (< 5 grams) per day
Maintain body mass index (BMI) within normal limits
Perform at least 30 minutes of aerobic exercise 5 days a week
Avoid smoking and limit alcohol intake
Practice stress-reduction techniques (meditation, yoga, deep breathing)
general_care_information: Monitor blood pressure routinely at home with a calibrated digital arm cuff
Take prescribed anti-hypertensive medications (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, Calcium Channel Blockers, Diuretics) regularly without skipping
Never stop medication when BP readings appear normal; the medication is what keeps the reading normal
Periodic monitoring of serum creatinine, electrolytes, and ECG
warning_signs: Hypertensive Crisis (BP > 180/120 mmHg): sudden thunderclap headache, blurred vision, acute chest pain, breathlessness, confusion, or weakness on one side of the face/arm (stroke warning)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek emergency medical evaluation immediately if blood pressure reads > 180/120 mmHg with any symptoms of chest pain, shortness of breath, or neurological deficits.
contraindications: Do NOT abruptly cease Beta-blockers or Clonidine; sudden withdrawal can trigger rebound hypertensive crises and myocardial infarction.

faqs.q: What is normal blood pressure?
faqs.a: Normal adult blood pressure is below 120/80 mmHg. Readings between 120-129/<80 are elevated; 130-139/80-89 is Stage 1 hypertension; ≥140/90 is Stage 2.

hi.name: उच्च रक्तचाप / हाई बीपी (Hypertension)
hi.overview: धमनियों में रक्त के दबाव का लगातार सामान्य से अधिक (140/90 या उससे ऊपर) रहना। इसे 'साइलेंट किलर' कहा जाता है।

te.name: అధిక రక్తపోటు / హై బీపీ
te.overview: ధమనులలో రక్త పీడనం నిరంతరం ఎక్కువగా ఉండే పరిస్థితి (140/90 mmHg పైన). దీనిని సైలెంట్ కిల్లర్ అంటారు.

name: Pneumonia
overview: Pneumonia is an acute inflammatory infection of one or both lungs that causes the alveoli (air sacs) to fill with pus, inflammatory exudate, and fluid, significantly impeding gas exchange.
common_symptoms: High fever with chills and rigor
Productive cough with yellow, green, or rust-colored sputum
Pleuritic chest pain (sharp stabbing pain when taking a deep breath or coughing)
Shortness of breath / rapid shallow breathing
Extreme fatigue, sweatiness, and loss of appetite
causes: Bacterial infection (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae)
Viral infection (RSV, Influenza, SARS-CoV-2)
Fungal or aspiration etiology
transmission: Inhalation of airborne pathogens or micro-aspiration of colonized oropharyngeal secretions
risk_factors: Smoking and COPD / chronic lung diseases
prevention: Pneumococcal conjugate / polysaccharide vaccination (PCV13 / PPSV23)
Annual influenza vaccination
Cessation of smoking and alcohol abuse
Good oral hygiene and pulmonary toilet
Hand hygiene in healthcare and community environments
general_care_information: Prompt medical consultation for chest auscultation and chest radiography
Complete the entire course of prescribed antibiotics or antiviral therapy
Adequate hydration to thin pulmonary secretions and facilitate coughing
Rest with upper torso elevated to improve lung expansion and diaphragmatic movement
warning_signs: Blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) < 92%
Severe dyspnea, cyanosis (bluish lips/fingers), or grunting respiration
Hypotension (systolic BP < 90 mmHg) or rapid heart rate (> 120 bpm)
New onset confusion, lethargy, or inability to stay awake
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek immediate hospital emergency admission if breathing is painful and rapid, or if SpO2 drops below 93%.
contraindications: Do not suppress a productive cough with strong cough sedatives without doctor consent; clearing phlegm is necessary to resolve alveolar consolidation.

faqs.q: Is pneumonia contagious?
faqs.a: The bacteria and viruses causing pneumonia can be transmitted via droplets, though not everyone infected will necessarily develop lung consolidation.

hi.name: निमोनिया (Pneumonia)
hi.overview: फेफड़ों के वायु थैलों (एल्वियोली) का गंभीर संक्रमण जिसमें मवाद और तरल पदार्थ भर जाता है।

te.name: న్యుమోనియా
te.overview: ఊపిరితిత్తులలో చీము మరియు ద్రవాలు చేరే తీవ్ర ఇన్ఫెక్షన్. శ్వాసలో నొప్పి, దగ్గు మరియు జ్వరం ఉంటాయి.

name: Hepatitis B
overview: Hepatitis B is a viral liver infection caused by the Hepatitis B virus (HBV) that can cause both acute illness and chronic liver disease, leading to progressive cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer).
common_symptoms: Abdominal pain in right upper quadrant (liver area)
Nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite
causes: Hepatitis B virus (HBV, Hepadnaviridae family)
transmission: Contact with infectious blood, semen, or other body fluids
Perinatal transmission from mother to baby during birth
Unsafe injections, unsterile tattoos, or sharing needles
Unprotected sexual intercourse
prevention: Hepatitis B vaccination (3-dose series) beginning at birth
Screening of all donated blood and blood products
Use of single-use disposable syringes and needles
Safe sex practices with barrier contraception
Standard infection control precautions in medical settings
general_care_information: Screening with HBsAg, anti-HBs, and HBV DNA viral load tests
Total avoidance of alcohol, hepatotoxic medications, and unverified herbal supplements
Well-balanced nutrition rich in fresh produce, lean protein, and adequate fluids
Regular liver function tests (LFT) and ultrasound screening for chronic carriers
warning_signs: Severe worsening jaundice with mental confusion (hepatic encephalopathy)
Ascites (distended fluid accumulation in the abdomen)
Hematemesis (vomiting blood from esophageal varices)
Spontaneous bleeding or bruising due to coagulopathy
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek immediate gastroenterological care if jaundice, pale stools, or dark urine appear, or if you suspect blood/body fluid exposure.
contraindications: Strictly avoid all alcohol consumption; avoid high doses of Paracetamol (> 2g/day) which can precipitate acute liver necrosis.

faqs.q: Can Hepatitis B be prevented by vaccine?
faqs.a: Yes! The Hepatitis B vaccine has over 98% efficacy in preventing infection and subsequent chronic liver cancer.

hi.name: हेपेटाइटिस बी / पीलिया (Hepatitis B)
hi.overview: हेपेटाइटिस बी वायरस से होने वाला गंभीर यकृत (लिवर) का संक्रमण, जिससे पीलिया और लिवर सिरोसिस हो सकता है।

te.name: హెపటైటిస్ బి / పచ్చకామెర్లు
te.overview: హెపటైటిస్ బి వైరస్ వల్ల కాలేయానికి వచ్చే తీవ్రమైన ఇన్ఫెక్షన్. మూత్రం పసుపు రంగులో రావడం ప్రధాన లక్షణం.

name: GERD (Acid Reflux)
overview: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) is a chronic digestive condition where stomach acid and enzyme-rich gastric contents repeatedly flow backward into the esophagus, causing chemical irritation and mucosal erosion.
common_symptoms: Heartburn (burning pain or discomfort in chest behind breastbone)
Acid regurgitation (sour or bitter fluid rising into throat or mouth)
Chronic dry cough or throat clearing
Sensation of a lump in the throat (globus sensation)
causes: Transient or chronic relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter (LES)
Hiatal hernia
Delayed gastric emptying
transmission: Non-communicable gastrointestinal disorder
risk_factors: Heavy meals before bedtime, fatty/fried foods, caffeine, chocolate, and citrus
prevention: Eat smaller, more frequent meals rather than large heavy dinners
Remain upright for at least 2 to 3 hours after eating; avoid reclining immediately
Elevate the head of your bed by 6 to 8 inches (using bed risers, not just extra pillows)
Limit trigger foods: deep fried foods, spicy curries, citrus, coffee, carbonated drinks, and raw onions
Maintain healthy body weight and avoid tight restrictive waistbands
general_care_information: Over-the-counter antacids or physician-prescribed PPIs (Omeprazole, Pantoprazole) or H2 blockers
Chew food thoroughly and eat in a relaxed unhurried environment
Avoid late-night snacking and drinking alcohol before bed
Drink adequate water during the day, but sip small amounts during meals
warning_signs: CRITICAL: Crushing chest pain radiating to jaw, left shoulder, or arm with cold sweats (must be evaluated as Myocardial Infarction / Heart Attack first!)
Progressive difficulty or pain when swallowing solid food
Vomiting coffee-ground material or blood
Unexplained weight loss or persistent choking spells at night
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek emergency medical care if chest pain is crushing or unfamiliar. Consult a gastroenterologist if heartburn occurs more than twice a week or if swallowing is impaired.
contraindications: Do NOT assume severe acute chest pressure is 'just acidity'; always rule out an acute cardiac event first.

faqs.q: How can I tell heart attack chest pain from GERD heartburn?
faqs.a: Heartburn is typically a burning retrosternal sensation worsened by lying down; heart attack pain is a heavy pressure, squeezing, or tightness often radiating to arm/jaw with breathlessness and cold sweats. When in doubt, seek emergency care immediately!

hi.name: जीईआरडी / एसिडिटी (GERD / Acid Reflux)
hi.overview: पेट का एसिड बार-बार भोजन नली में वापस आने से सीने में जलन (हार्टबर्न) और खट्टी डकारें आना।

te.name: గ్యాస్ / ఎసిడిటీ (GERD)
te.overview: కడుపులోని ఆమ్లాలు అన్నవాహికలోకి తిరిగి రావడం వల్ల ఛాతీలో మంట, పుల్లని తేన్పులు రావడం.

name: Iron-Deficiency Anemia
overview: Iron-deficiency anemia is a common blood condition characterized by a deficit of functional iron, leading to reduced hemoglobin synthesis and diminished oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.
common_symptoms: Pale or yellowish skin, inner eyelids, and pale nail beds
Shortness of breath with minimal exertion
Craving non-food items like ice, chalk, or clay (pica)
causes: Inadequate dietary iron intake
Chronic blood loss (heavy menstrual periods, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcers, hookworm infestation)
Impaired iron absorption (celiac disease, post-bariatric surgery)
transmission: Non-communicable hematological nutritional condition
risk_factors: Strict vegetarian/vegan diets without balanced iron planning
prevention: Consume iron-rich foods: dark green leafy vegetables (spinach, methi), lentils, chickpeas, beans, nuts, seeds, jaggery, eggs, and lean meats
Pair iron foods with Vitamin C (lemon juice, amla, oranges, tomatoes) which enhances iron absorption significantly
Avoid drinking strong tea or coffee directly with meals, as tannins inhibit iron uptake
Routine screening in adolescent girls and pregnant women
Regular deworming in endemic areas
general_care_information: Complete blood count (CBC), serum ferritin, and iron profile tests
Take prescribed oral iron supplements (e.g. Ferrous ascorbate/fumarate) as directed, ideally with vitamin C on an empty stomach or with a light snack if gastric upset occurs
Do not consume milk, calcium supplements, or antacids within 2 hours of taking iron tablets
Expect harmless dark stools while taking oral iron
warning_signs: Chest pain, palpitations, or fainting spells upon standing
Severe breathlessness even at complete rest
Tarry black stools or visible blood in stools (indicative of acute GI bleed)
Hemoglobin falling below 7.0 g/dL
when_to_seek_medical_help: Consult a physician for blood tests if you experience persistent fatigue or pallor. Seek emergency care if fainting, chest pain, or severe breathlessness occurs.
contraindications: Do not take iron supplements without confirming deficiency via blood tests; iron overload (hemochromatosis) damages liver and heart.

faqs.q: What is normal hemoglobin level?
faqs.a: Normal Hb for adult males is 13.8 to 17.2 g/dL; for non-pregnant adult females, it is 12.1 to 15.1 g/dL.

hi.name: एनीमिया / खून की कमी (Anemia)
hi.overview: आयरन की कमी के कारण हीमोग्लोबिन कम होना, जिससे कमजोरी, थकान और त्वचा में पीलापन होता है।

te.name: రక్తహీనత (ఎనీమియా)
te.overview: శరీరంలో ఐరన్ లోపం వల్ల హిమోగ్లోబిన్ తగ్గడం. నీరసం, అలసట, తలతిరగడం ప్రధాన లక్షణాలు.

name: Dehydration & Heat Exhaustion
overview: Dehydration occurs when the body loses significantly more water and essential electrolytes than it takes in, impairing normal cellular and physiological functions, frequently triggered by heatwaves, fever, vomiting, or diarrhea.
common_symptoms: Dry sticky mouth and cracked lips
Fatigue, weakness, and lightheadedness upon standing
causes: Insufficient fluid intake during hot weather or strenuous exercise
Excessive sweating, prolonged fever, or gastrointestinal fluid loss (vomiting, diarrhea)
transmission: Non-communicable environmental/physiological condition
risk_factors: Infants and young children (high surface-area-to-mass ratio)
Elderly individuals with blunted thirst mechanisms
Outdoor manual laborers and athletes in high temperatures
prevention: Drink plenty of water consistently throughout the day (at least 2.5 to 3 liters daily)
Drink extra fluids before, during, and after physical exertion or outdoor exposure
Consume hydrating foods: watermelons, cucumbers, tender coconut water, buttermilk, and soups
Avoid excessive alcohol and sugary drinks which worsen fluid loss
Rest in shaded, ventilated spaces during peak sunshine hours (11 AM to 4 PM)
general_care_information: Sip Oral Rehydration Salt (ORS) solution slowly in small frequent gulps
Move to a cool, air-conditioned or shaded room and loosen tight clothing
Apply cool wet cloths to the forehead, neck, and underarms
Monitor urine color: aim for pale straw yellow
warning_signs: Severe Heat Stroke / Hypovolemia: Core body temperature > 103°F (39.4°C)
Hot, red, completely dry skin without sweating
Confusion, slurred speech, delirium, or loss of consciousness
Inability to retain any oral fluids due to persistent vomiting
No urination for more than 8 hours
when_to_seek_medical_help: EMERGENCY: If heat stroke symptoms, confusion, or zero urine output develop, call 108 immediately and begin aggressive evaporative external cooling while awaiting transport.
contraindications: Do not administer salt tablets or concentrated sugary drinks without water; they can exacerbate hyperosmolar dehydration.

faqs.q: How to prepare WHO ORS at home?
faqs.a: Dissolve 1 standard packet of WHO ORS powder in exactly 1 liter of clean drinking water. If unavailable in an emergency, mix 6 level teaspoons of sugar and 1/2 level teaspoon of salt in 1 liter of clean water.

hi.name: डिहाइड्रेशन / निर्जलीकरण (Dehydration)
hi.overview: शरीर में पानी और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स की अत्यधिक कमी होना। चक्कर आना और गहरा पेशाब इसके लक्षण हैं।

te.name: నిర్జలీకరణం / డీహైడ్రేషన్
te.overview: శరీరంలో తగినంత నీరు మరియు లవణాలు తగ్గడం. తీవ్రమైన దాహం, తలనొప్పి, మూత్రం తక్కువ రావడం లక్షణాలు.

name: Common Cold
overview: The common cold is a mild, self-limiting viral infection of the upper respiratory tract primarily caused by Rhinoviruses. It causes nasal discharge, congestion, and mild sore throat.
causes: Rhinovirus (over 50% of cases), Coronavirus, Adenovirus
transmission: Inhalation of airborne droplets from coughing/sneezing
Touching contaminated surfaces and touching eyes, nose, or mouth
risk_factors: Young children in school or daycare
prevention: Wash hands frequently with soap and water for 20 seconds
Avoid touching eyes, nose, and mouth with unwashed hands
Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or elbow
Stay home while symptomatic to protect vulnerable individuals
Disinfect high-touch objects (doorknobs, mobile screens)
general_care_information: Adequate rest and high intake of warm fluids (herbal teas, warm water, soups)
Saline nasal spray or drops to loosen nasal mucus
Steam inhalation for nasal decongestion
Warm salt water gargle (1/2 tsp salt in 1 cup warm water) for throat soothing
warning_signs: Fever > 102°F or fever lasting more than 3-4 days
Shortness of breath, chest pain, or wheezing
Severe sinus pain around forehead and cheekbones lasting > 10 days
when_to_seek_medical_help: Consult a doctor if cold symptoms persist longer than 10-14 days without improvement, or if breathing becomes labored.
contraindications: Do NOT demand or use antibiotics for a common cold; antibiotics have zero effect on cold viruses.

faqs.q: How long does a typical cold last?
faqs.a: Most common colds resolve naturally within 7 to 10 days with basic rest and supportive hydration.

hi.name: सामान्य सर्दी-जुकाम (Common Cold)
hi.overview: राइनोवायरस से होने वाला हल्का ऊपरी श्वसन संक्रमण जिसमें छींकें, बहती नाक और गले में खराश होती है।

te.name: సాధారణ జలుబు
te.overview: ముక్కు కారడం, తుమ్ములు మరియు గొంతు నొప్పి కలిగించే సాధారణ వైరల్ ఇన్ఫెక్షన్.

name: Chickenpox (Varicella)
overview: Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral illness caused by the varicella-zoster virus (VZV), characterized by an intensely itchy blister-like rash starting on the chest, back, and face, spreading across the entire body.
common_symptoms: Itchy fluid-filled blisters (vesicles) on red base
causes: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection
transmission: Direct contact with blister fluid
Airborne droplet transmission when an infected person coughs or breathes
risk_factors: Close contact with active chickenpox or shingles patients
prevention: Varicella vaccination (2-dose series for children and non-immune adults)
Isolate the infected person until all blisters have scabbed over completely (usually 7 days)
Avoid scratching blisters to prevent secondary bacterial skin infections (staph/strep)
Good hand hygiene for caregivers
general_care_information: Apply calamine lotion to itchy lesions
Take cool or lukewarm oatmeal baths to soothe cutaneous itching
Keep fingernails trimmed short and clean to minimize skin trauma from scratching
Paracetamol for fever; consult a pediatrician for oral antihistamines
warning_signs: Skin rash becomes very red, warm, tender, or leaks yellow pus (secondary bacterial superinfection)
Extreme drowsiness, confusion, unsteady gait, or stiff neck
Persistent coughing or difficulty breathing (varicella pneumonia)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek medical care if a newborn, pregnant woman, or immunocompromised individual is exposed, or if any warning signs develop.
contraindications: NEVER give Aspirin to anyone with chickenpox; this can trigger Reye's syndrome (fatal liver and brain swelling).

faqs.q: Can someone get chickenpox twice?
faqs.a: Rarely. Infection usually provides lifelong immunity, though the dormant virus can reactivate decades later as Shingles (Herpes Zoster).

hi.name: चेचक / छोटी माता (Chickenpox)
hi.overview: वेरिसेला-जोस्टर वायरस से फैलने वाला अत्यधिक संक्रामक रोग जिसमें पूरे शरीर पर खुजली वाले दाने और छाले निकलते हैं।

te.name: ఆటలమ్మ / చికెన్ పాక్స్
te.overview: వైరస్ వల్ల ఒంటిపై నీటి పొక్కులు, దురద మరియు జ్వరం కలిగించే అంటువ్యాధి.

name: Measles (Rubeola)
overview: Measles is a highly contagious, serious airborne viral disease caused by a paramyxovirus. It spreads easily through the air when an infected person breathes, coughs, or sneezes.
common_symptoms: The 3 C's: Cough, Coryza (runny nose), and Conjunctivitis (red, watery eyes)
Koplik spots (tiny white spots with bluish-white centers inside the mouth)
Maculopapular rash starting at hairline and spreading downward
causes: Measles virus (Morbillivirus genus, Paramyxoviridae family)
transmission: Airborne aerosol transmission; virus can remain suspended in air and infectious for up to 2 hours after an infected person leaves the room
prevention: MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella) vaccine (2 doses provide 97% lifetime protection)
Strict isolation of suspected cases for at least 4 days after the rash appears
Vitamin A supplementation in children diagnosed with measles as per WHO guidelines
Maintain high community vaccination coverage (>95% herd immunity)
general_care_information: Bed rest in a dimly lit room to protect eyes from bright light
Adequate fluid intake (ORS, juices, water) to avoid dehydration
Paracetamol for fever relief
WHO-recommended high-dose Vitamin A administration under medical supervision
warning_signs: Severe persistent coughing or fast breathing (measles pneumonia)
Ear pain or purulent drainage (acute otitis media)
Extreme lethargy, convulsions, or stiff neck (measles encephalitis)
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek immediate medical attention if measles is suspected, particularly in infants under 12 months or individuals with breathing difficulty.
contraindications: Do not administer aspirin to pediatric patients due to risk of Reye's syndrome.

faqs.q: How contagious is measles?
faqs.a: Measles is one of the world's most contagious diseases: one infected individual can infect up to 9 out of 10 unvaccinated close contacts.

hi.name: खसरा (Measles)
hi.overview: हवा से फैलने वाला अत्यधिक संक्रामक वायरल रोग जिसमें तेज बुखार, खांसी और त्वचा पर लाल दाने होते हैं।

te.name: తట్టు / మీజిల్స్
te.overview: గాలి ద్వారా వ్యాపించే అత్యంత తీవ్రమైన వైరల్ వ్యాధి. తీవ్ర జ్వరం, ఎర్రటి దద్దుర్లు దీని ప్రధాన లక్షణాలు.

name: Food Poisoning (Acute Foodborne Illness)
overview: Food poisoning is an acute illness caused by consuming food or beverages contaminated with infectious bacteria, viruses, parasites, or their toxins (such as Salmonella, E. coli, Staphylococcus aureus, or Norovirus).
common_symptoms: Acute abdominal cramps and stomach pain
causes: Bacterial toxins (Staph enterotoxin, B. cereus)
Bacterial infection (Salmonella, Campylobacter, E. coli)
Viral infection (Norovirus, Rotavirus)
transmission: Ingesting undercooked meats, unpasteurized milk, contaminated dairy, or raw salads washed with tainted water
Cross-contamination in kitchens
risk_factors: Eating raw seafood, undercooked eggs, or street foods left unrefrigerated
prevention: Cook all poultry, ground meats, and eggs to safe internal temperatures
Refrigerate perishable foods promptly within 2 hours of preparation
Wash cutting boards, knives, and countertops with hot soapy water after handling raw meats
Keep raw meats and fresh ready-to-eat produce completely separate
Drink only treated, boiled, or purified water
general_care_information: Rest the stomach for a few hours, then sip clear fluids or ORS slowly in small teaspoons
Gradually reintroduce bland foods (BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast)
Avoid dairy products, caffeine, alcohol, nicotine, and high-fat spicy dishes for 48 hours
Replace lost electrolytes to prevent hypovolemic dehydration
warning_signs: Inability to keep liquids down for more than 12-24 hours
Blood in vomit or bloody stools
Signs of severe dehydration: dry mouth, minimal urination, dizziness, sunken eyes
High fever (>102°F) accompanied by severe abdominal pain
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek immediate medical attention if diarrhea lasts more than 3 days, if stools contain visible blood, or if symptoms of dehydration occur.
contraindications: Do NOT use anti-motility drugs (like Loperamide) if diarrhea is accompanied by high fever or bloody stools, as they trap invasive pathogens in the intestine.

faqs.q: How fast does food poisoning begin?
faqs.a: Toxin-mediated food poisoning (Staph aureus) can start within 1 to 6 hours; bacterial infections (Salmonella) usually take 12 to 72 hours to manifest.

hi.name: फूड पॉइजनिंग / खाद्य विषाक्तता
hi.overview: दूषित या बासी भोजन खाने से होने वाली बीमारी, जिसमें पेट दर्द, उल्टी और दस्त होते हैं।

te.name: ఫుడ్ పాయిజనింగ్
te.overview: కలుషిత ఆహారం తినడం వల్ల కడుపునొప్పి, వాంతులు, విరేచనాలు కలిగించే తీవ్రమైన పరిస్థితి.

name: Hepatitis A
overview: Hepatitis A is a highly contagious liver infection caused by the Hepatitis A virus (HAV). Unlike Hepatitis B and C, it does not cause chronic liver disease and is rarely fatal, but can cause debilitating symptoms.
common_symptoms: Loss of appetite and aversion to oily food
Nausea, vomiting, and upper right abdominal pain
causes: Hepatitis A virus (HAV, Picornaviridae family)
transmission: Fecal-oral route through ingestion of water or food contaminated with feces of an infected person
Direct close contact with an infected family member
risk_factors: Poor community sanitation and contaminated water pipes
Eating raw shellfish harvested from sewage-polluted waters
prevention: Hepatitis A vaccination (2 doses 6 months apart)
Rigorous handwashing with soap before eating and after using the toilet
Drink only boiled or purified water
Avoid raw salads, unpeeled fruits, and street vendors' drinks in endemic zones
Adequate municipal sewage treatment
general_care_information: Rest during the acute icteric (jaundice) phase until appetite returns
High-carbohydrate, low-fat nutritious diet that is gentle on liver metabolism (fruit juices, rice, khichdi, honey)
Strictly avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic drugs (like Paracetamol in high doses)
Frequent hydration to support metabolic clearance
warning_signs: Severe persistent vomiting resulting in dehydration
Confusion, extreme drowsiness, or hand tremors (acute liver failure)
Prolonged severe jaundice lasting more than 4 weeks
when_to_seek_medical_help: Consult a physician when jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools appear for diagnostic liver function tests (LFT) and viral serology.
contraindications: Strictly avoid all alcohol consumption during illness and for at least 6 months after recovery.

faqs.q: Does Hepatitis A turn into chronic liver disease?
faqs.a: No, Hepatitis A almost never becomes chronic. The body typically clears the virus completely and develops lifelong protective immunity.

name: Migraine Headache
overview: Migraine is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by recurrent attacks of moderate to severe throbbing or pulsating unilateral headache, often accompanied by autonomic, visual, and sensory symptoms.
common_symptoms: Unilateral throbbing or pulsating head pain (one side of head)
Visual aura (zigzag flashing lights, blind spots 20-30 mins prior)
Pain worsened by routine physical activity
causes: Neurovascular dysfunction, trigeminovascular activation, and cortical spreading depression
transmission: Non-communicable neurological disorder
risk_factors: Female sex (3x more common in women due to hormonal fluctuations)
Stress, irregular sleep, skipping meals, caffeine withdrawal, sensory stimuli (bright lights, perfumes), artificial sweeteners
prevention: Maintain a consistent sleep-wake schedule 7 days a week
Do not skip meals; keep blood sugar stable with balanced snacks
Stay well-hydrated throughout the day
Keep a headache diary to identify individual triggers (chocolate, aged cheese, MSG, wine)
Physician-prescribed preventive medications (Beta-blockers, Topiramate, Flunarizine) for frequent debilitating attacks
general_care_information: Rest in a quiet, dark, well-ventilated room during an attack
Apply a cold ice compress or cool gel pack to the forehead or back of the neck
Take abortive medication (such as Paracetamol/NSAIDs or prescribed Triptans) at the earliest onset of pain
Sip water or electrolyte fluids
warning_signs: 'Thunderclap' headache: instantaneous peak intensity within seconds (rule out Subarachnoid Hemorrhage!)
Headache accompanied by high fever, stiff neck, confusion, or rash (rule out Meningitis!)
New onset focal weakness, speech difficulty, or facial drooping (rule out Stroke!)
First severe headache onset after age 50
when_to_seek_medical_help: Seek emergency medical evaluation if a sudden explosive headache occurs or is accompanied by neurological deficits. Consult a neurologist for recurring headaches.
contraindications: Do NOT overuse abortive pain medications (> 10-15 days/month) as this causes Medication Overuse Headache (rebound headaches).

faqs.q: What is a migraine aura?
faqs.a: An aura is a temporary neurological disturbance, usually visual (flashing lights, zigzag lines, or vision loss), occurring 20–60 minutes before the headache begins.

hi.name: माइग्रेन / आधासीसी का दर्द

name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
overview: Chronic Kidney Disease is a progressive, long-term condition where the kidneys become damaged and cannot filter toxins, excess metabolic waste, and excess fluids from the blood effectively.
common_symptoms: Often completely asymptomatic in early stages
Swelling (edema) in feet, ankles, legs, or puffiness around eyes
Fatigue and decreased mental sharpness due to anemia
Changes in urination (foamy/bubbly urine, frequent night urination)
Loss of appetite, metallic taste in mouth, nausea
Difficulty breathing due to fluid buildup in lungs
causes: Longstanding uncontrolled diabetes (Diabetic Nephropathy)
Uncontrolled hypertension (Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis)
Glomerulonephritis, Polycystic kidney disease, recurrent kidney infections
transmission: Non-communicable chronic disease
risk_factors: Frequent long-term use of NSAID pain relievers (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac)
prevention: Strictly maintain blood pressure target (usually < 130/80 mmHg)
Strictly control blood sugar (HbA1c target < 7.0%) in diabetics
Avoid regular over-the-counter NSAID painkillers which are nephrotoxic
Maintain a low-sodium diet (< 2g sodium/day) and avoid excess protein supplements
Annual screening of serum creatinine, eGFR, and urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio (ACR)
general_care_information: Consult a nephrologist for individualized disease staging (Stages 1 to 5)
Follow prescribed dietary restrictions regarding sodium, potassium, and phosphorus
Stay well-hydrated within personal fluid limits advised by doctor
Take ACE-inhibitors or ARBs as prescribed to protect glomeruli
warning_signs: Severe shortness of breath or inability to lie flat (pulmonary edema)
Severe confusion, drowsiness, or seizures (uremic encephalopathy)
Critically elevated serum potassium (> 6.0 mEq/L - cardiac arrest danger)
Zero urine output (anuria) over 12 hours
when_to_seek_medical_help: Consult a physician if you notice leg swelling or foamy urine. Seek emergency care immediately if severe breathlessness or confusion develops in a CKD patient.
contraindications: Strictly avoid NSAIDs (Diclofenac, Ibuprofen, Naproxen); use only Paracetamol for minor pain with doctor permission.

faqs.q: What test checks kidney function?
faqs.a: Serum Creatinine with estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) and a simple Urine Routine / Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (ACR).
